page_title: gadak — Query your Jira backlog with SQL

summary.name: gadak
summary.one_liner: gadak mirrors chosen Jira Cloud projects and Confluence spaces into a local SQLite file so you can search and query them with SQL, offline, and give a coding agent the same data.
use_cases: count open issues per epic in a Jira backlog
search Jira issues and Confluence pages offline
give a coding agent read access to Jira data
analyze Jira change history with SQL
create or transition Jira issues from the terminal
browse a local Jira mirror on a desktop or in a browser tab
summary.what_it_does: gadak syncs the Jira Cloud projects and Confluence spaces you select into one SQLite file on your machine, including issue titles, bodies, comments and wiki pages, and searches that file without a network connection. You can run SQL over the file to answer aggregate questions that JQL cannot express, such as counts grouped by epic. The desktop app, browser tab, CLI and coding agents (via a Claude Code skill or an MCP server) all read the same file. Writes such as comments, transitions and assignments go to Jira first, and the local cache refreshes after Jira accepts them.
notable: Local SQLite mirror of Jira Cloud and Confluence with SQL queries and offline search
Write-through: changes go to Jira first, and nothing is queued locally
Works as a Claude Code skill and Claude Desktop MCP server, reading the same local file
Apache-2.0 licensed, single maintainer, no telemetry or gadak account according to the page
caveats: Status is 0.24 (still 0.x); iOS app is in beta with TestFlight internal testers only and no public download
Requires a local binary and an initial sync; reads trail Jira by one sync interval
Confluence Server has no client, so Server workspaces mirror issues only; Jira Server/Data Center needs a personal access token
